problemStatement.formal: N_{\le r}(n,k) = \sum_{j=0}^{k} (-1)^j \binom{k}{j}\binom{n - j(r+1) + k - 1}{k-1}, \quad \text{where } \binom{m}{k-1}=0 \text{ for } m<k-1.
problemStatement.plain: Count the ways to put $n$ identical balls into $k$ labelled boxes when no box may hold more than $r$ balls. Stars-and-bars gives $\binom{n+k-1}{k-1}$ without the cap; the cap is enforced by an alternating inclusion–exclusion correction that subtracts overflow, adds back double-overflow, and so on. Prove the closed form, recovering the uncapped count when $r \ge n$.

insights: Bounded count N_{<=r}(n,k) = #{f:Fin k->N // (sum f=n) and forall i, f i<=r}; cleanest to define as a Finset.filter over the parent (finite) weak-composition type rather than a fresh subtype of Fin k->N (which is infinite).

SUBTLETY (key): the alternating closed form must live in Z, and the convention C(m,k-1)=0 for m<k-1 CANNOT be emulated with truncated N subtraction in the binomial argument. Writing top as n - j*(r+1) in N truncates to 0 when j(r+1)>n, giving C(k-1,k-1)=1 != 0 -- wrong already at k=1 (the j=1 term would spuriously cancel j=0 for admissible n<=r). Faithful rendering: guard each term by j*(r+1) <= n.
Closed form is only meaningful for k>=1: at k=0 the k-1 N-truncation makes C(...,0)=1 spuriously, so boundedRHS_of_le is FALSE for k=0,n>=1. Main theorem and RHS-recovery both carry hk:0<k.

Recovery direction (n<=r): the cap is vacuous since each part f i <= sum f = n <= r (Finset.single_le_sum), so the filter is trivially total and boundedCount = C(n+k-1,n) (parent card_weakComposition). Fully proved (hand-authored, build-pending).
RHS collapse (n<=r): for j>=1, j(r+1)>=r+1>n so the guard fails and the term is dropped; only j=0 survives = C(n+k-1,k-1)=C(n+k-1,n) via Nat.choose_symm. Fully proved via Finset.sum_eq_single 0.

IE strategy for the open core: U = all weak comps (|U|=C(n+k-1,k-1)); bad event A_i = {f i >= r+1}; admissible = U minus union A_i; |A_S| for |S|=j via shift bijection (subtract r+1 on S-coords) = C(n-j(r+1)+k-1,k-1); group 2^k subsets by size j (C(k,j) each) -> the stated single sum.
